answer: Every new agent must escrow a bond that vests only on a glacier schedule, so a Sybil farm cannot buy a thousand identities and cash out next epoch: it pays the full bond for each one and waits. Membership also enters through a narrow inlet, a hard cap on fresh identities per epoch priced by demand, so mass creation costs more than honest growth. Reputation compounds only on an established knoll of prior attested work, and any cluster whose peer attestations collapse forfeits the entire escrow. The attacker's cost is the sum of every bond, paid up front and lost on detection.
